lessons.title: Giveaways, doubling, and “send 1 get 2”
lessons.content:
# Giveaways, doubling, and “send 1 get 2”

If a stranger asks you to **send first** to receive more, you are the donor. The chain will record a gift. It will not record a contract you thought you had. There is no parent to call.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to name a send-first bonus as a donation, refuse a “whitelist snapshot” that wants a transfer, and not send a second time to “unlock” the first.

## Why it still works

It copies a real pattern. Companies run promotions. Networks run **airdrops** — unsolicited token distributions — sometimes honestly, often as bait (Module 4). The honest versions, when they exist, do not need you to fund a “verification wallet.” They do not need a seed. They do not need you to pay gas to a helper.

The scam adds a payment. The payment is the scam. Screenshots of “last ten winners” are recycled. Telegram badges are self-awarded. A countdown is a prop. Live video of a “founder” can be a costume or a deepfake; you still do not send first.

People send because the amount looks small (“it’s only 1 USDT”) and because refusing feels like leaving money on the table. Practice-amount rules still apply: small is how they train the yes. After the yes, the number grows.

## Crystal Stones flavour, said without a buy order

“Send CST to this address to whitelist for the snapshot.” “Double CST for 30 minutes, official.” “Gas fee to this helper so the airdrop can land.” Unless you independently verify a **slow, public** process on channels you already trusted *before* the message — bookmarked site, not a new contract in a DM — this is Door 4 plus Door 4’s invoice.

The contract to verify, if you are looking at Crystal Stones at all, remains:

`0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00`

A doubling address is not that contract. A “new CST” with a similar name is a clone. This academy will not tell you a snapshot is coming. Anyone who knows a snapshot “from inside the academy” and needs your send is not inside the academy.

## What the explorer will show, and what it will not

BscScan (bookmarked) will show many incoming transfers to one ordinary address — an **EOA**, an externally owned account, a person-shaped wallet, not a published programme with rules you can read. It will not show outgoing doubles of any honest size. The book is public. The hope was not.

You cannot “report to the chain” to reverse this. You can warn others with the destination address and the domain. You must not chase with a second send to “unlock the first.” Unlock is the same script in a second costume. You must not send leftover dust to a recovery specialist who appeared in the same group. That is Module 5’s second predator.

TABLE
Promise | Reality | Door
Send 1 BNB, get 2 | You send 1, they send 0 | Human, then a send
Pay gas to this helper | They take the gas | Human, then a send
Last 10 winners, screenshotted | Recycled images | Human
Verified badge in Telegram | Self-awarded costume | Human
“Whitelist for snapshot, send CST” | Donation unless a slow public process you already trusted | Human
“Send again, first tx is stuck” | Second donation | Human, panic
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** An X account cloned the project, same avatar, extra underscore. “Double CST for 30 minutes.” Three students in a WhatsApp stall-owners group send 20 USDT each because “it’s a small test.”

1. Bookmarked BscScan shows many incoming transfers to one EOA, no outgoing doubles of 40.
2. The book agrees they donated. Agreement is not comfort. It is clarity.
3. One student wants to send a fourth payment “because maybe the minimum was 50.” That is the trained yes, growing. The others stop him with this lesson, not with a whitepaper.
4. They warn the stall group with the fake handle and the destination, not with their remaining addresses. They do not open a bounty in DMs.

DIAGRAM
Send-first giveaway
        |
        v
Their ordinary address (EOA)
        |
        v
They leave
        |
        v
Explorer agrees you donated

There is no second send that unlocks the first.
There is no chain ticket that reverses a valid gift.
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
Charity is allowed. You may give. Call it a gift so your head stays honest. What is not allowed in this academy’s classroom is mistaking a gift for a contract, a doubling, a whitelist, or a validator reward. BNB validators are not paying you 2-for-1 in a DM.
ENDNOTE

Live video does not change the rule. A founder-shaped face on a stream can still be a costume or a deepfake, and even a real person can be impersonated in the replies under the stream. You still do not send first. You still verify a contract on a bookmark. The stream is Door 4 with better lighting.

## What this lesson is for

So that “small, official, hurry” stops looking like a promotion. Send-first is the whole tell. You do not need a forensic lab. You need the refusal. If a group calls you a tourist for refusing, they priced your USDT as an entry ticket. You can be a tourist who still has rent.

## Say this out loud

- Send-first bonuses are donations. The explorer will agree I donated.
- Badges in chats are not courts. Recycled winner screenshots are not audits.
- I do not send a second time to unlock the first.
- Crystal Stones snapshots, if they ever existed in public, would not start as a DM that needs my USDT.
- I can warn others with a domain and a destination. I do not post my remaining address as a trophy.

If you already sent, do not send again to “complete the bonus.” The explorer will not sprout a refund because you were polite the second time. Warn with the destination. Keep the rest.

Next: impersonation — founders, this academy, exchange support, and a “Crystal Mentor” who DMed first.

lessons.title: Impersonation: founders, academy, exchange support, “Crystal Mentor”
lessons.content:
# Impersonation: founders, academy, exchange support, “Crystal Mentor”

The account looks like someone you already trust. That is the entire trick. They do not need a new story. They need a used face.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to say how official contact actually starts, why pain in public is bait, and which test real staff will pass: they will leave WhatsApp for the bookmarked app.

## Where they sit

- replies under a real post (you think the founder replied)
- DMs after you comment “withdrawal stuck” or “seed help”
- WhatsApp using a similar display name and the academy crystal
- “Crystal Stones Academy Mentor” with a star they bought
- a cloned X or Telegram handle with an extra underscore, extra letter, or extra “official”
- a “Binance support” desk that arrived as a reply — Binance remaining **an example of a centralised exchange**, not the only desk that gets cloned

They will have the logo. They will have tone. They will have a case number. Case numbers are free.

## How official contact actually starts

You messaged **them** first from a bookmark, or you already have an in-app thread that started **inside** the product. You never rely on a display name alone. You never rely on a “verified” mark inside Telegram. You never rely on a PDF ID. You never rely on “I can see your user id, prove you are you by sending 2FA.”

Academy: you logged into the bookmarked app. Mentor is in-app. Staff who cannot finish a security conversation there are not staff.

Exchange support: you opened a ticket in the bookmarked app. Real desks do not start in a DM after you tweeted pain. They may email from an address you can check *after* you open the bookmarked site, not before.

Project news: channels you saved before the drama, cross-checked against the bookmarked site. A new “founder” live-stream with a claim link is drama, not news.

## What impersonators ask (all four doors)

Seeds and “sync phrases” (Door 1). 2FA, OTPs, “confirm this login” (Door 2). A new contract to add, a connect-and-sign (Door 3). A small verifying payment, a screen share, a the checkout processor QR, “the academy is late, use this checkout” (Door 4).

The refuse-line does not change with the costume. Compare the ask to the never-list from Module 1. First list: no. You do not need to authenticate the stranger. You need to refuse the ask.

A useful test you can say out loud: “I will continue inside the bookmarked app.” If they cannot follow, the conversation is over. If they get angry, that anger is data. Official desks do not need your cortisol. Costumes do.

TABLE
Channel | How official contact starts | How the costume starts
Academy | You logged into the bookmarked app | A DM, a WhatsApp, a Mentor who wants a seed
Exchange support | You opened a ticket in the bookmarked app | A reply-guy after you posted pain
Project news | Channels you saved before the drama | A new handle during the drama
Wallet vendor | Store listing / maker site you bookmarked | “Support” that needs the words to help
the checkout processor / tuition | Checkout you started in the academy site | Invoice in a chat
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** A student tweets at an exchange because a withdrawal is pending. A reply-guy with a helpdesk logo DMs a ticket URL. The student types email, password, and an OTP. The whitelist was off. The IOU left.

1. Real support never started in that DM. Pain in public is impersonator bait. The reply is not a coincidence. It is a job.
2. Door 2 opened. The fix is the parent’s security page from a bookmark: kill sessions, rotate password, rotate 2FA, check recent withdrawals. Not a second ticket from a second reply-guy.
3. If anything remains, whitelist goes on. The delay that annoyed them last month is the delay that would have saved the IOU.
4. They do not post “I got hacked, who can help?” next. That post is a dinner bell.

DIAGRAM
You posted pain
        |
        v
Many logos appear
        |
        v
Official path is still: you open the bookmark
        |
        X  you open the DM
        X  you send 2FA
        X  you "verify by sending USDT"
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
Staff of this academy should be willing to say: “I will not finish this in WhatsApp. Open the site.” If “staff” refuses to leave WhatsApp, they are not staff. If “Crystal Mentor” needs a seed to sync, it is not Mentor. If “listing team” needs a personal send, it is not a listing team. Use the test. Do not use a debate.
ENDNOTE

Voice notes and “I am in a meeting, just send the OTP” are still Door 2. Familiar audio is cheaper than it used to be. Call a number you already had. If you cannot, you wait. An OTP expires. A stolen session lasts until you kill it.

## What this lesson is for

So that familiarity stops being evidence. Faces are cheap. Official paths are narrow on purpose. Narrow is how you stay solvent. If a founder-shaped account DMs first, you do not owe them a reply that keeps Door 4 open. Bookmark or nothing is still the whole test.

## Say this out loud

- Display names are costumes. Verified ticks in a chat app are not courts.
- Official contact starts from a bookmark I already had, or from a thread I started inside the product.
- Pain in public is impersonator bait. I do not finish support in the reply.
- Real staff will leave WhatsApp for the official app. If they will not, they are not staff.
- I do not send 2FA, seeds, or USDT to a desk that DMed first.

Speed after you posted pain is not customer care. It is a job. The official desk is still the bookmark you already had, even if twenty logos arrived first.

Next: jobs, tasks, romance, and long cons — the scams that take weeks and pay a small withdrawal first so you will fund the large one.

lessons.title: Jobs, tasks, romance, and long cons
lessons.content:
# Jobs, tasks, romance, and long cons

Not every scam is a 30-second phish. Some take weeks. They pay a small withdrawal so you will fund a large one. They use unemployment, loneliness, and the wish to be competent. Naming the script is not mockery. It is how you step off it.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to refuse a task mill, refuse a secret earnings partnership, and treat a lover who is also your broker as a script — not as a special exception because the voice notes felt real.

## Task mills and “crypto jobs”

“We deposit, you trade, you keep a cut.” “Complete 20 tasks, withdraw at the end.” “HR hired you to test a Crystal Stones earnings dApp — don’t tell the academy, it is a secret partnership.”

Early withdrawals sometimes **work**. That is the bait. The large withdrawal is blocked until you pay a tax, a fee, an “AML unfreeze,” a “gas top-up,” a “tier upgrade.” You are funding them. The painted numbers on the private website are not BscScan.

There is also **mule** risk. If real stolen USDT moved through your KYC-facing account, your name is on a pipe. “I was only doing tasks” is not a shield you want to test. Refuse the job. Do not forward other people’s coins for a cut.

A real employer who needs you to hold keys, install an APK, or share a screen on day one is not a real employer. Real work can wait for a contract you can read, on a domain you can bookmark, without a seed.

## Romance as a door, before the next lesson’s folklore

A new friend. Patient. Not asking for money at first. Then a “safe platform” they will teach you. Then a withdrawal that needs one more deposit. The patience is the product. It is Door 4 with a calendar.

You do not owe a stranger your broker slot because they listened. You do not owe a voice note a USDT transfer. If a romance is also your only trading desk, you do not have a romance. The next lesson names **pig butchering** as the wider folklore. Today: the job/task/lover cluster is one family. Small out, large in.

## Secret partnerships with this academy

There are none that need your silence and your deposit. Intermediate and Advanced, when you choose them, are published tracks with published checkout. There is no underground Crystal Stones earnings dApp that staff will deny in public and confirm in WhatsApp. “Don’t tell the academy” is a complete tell. You can refuse without a whitepaper.

TABLE
Pattern | Early feeling | The invoice | Adult move
Task mill | Small withdraw works; you feel hired | Tax / AML / tier to take the large amount | Stop depositing; do not pay the tax
Secret “test the dApp” job | Chosen, insider | Approve or send | Secrets + earnings + do-not-tell = no
Romance-broker | Patience, flattery | Private painted platform | Lover who is also broker is a script
Guaranteed club (preview) | Community | Recruit or deposit more | Guarantees are a tell; next lessons
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** A “HR manager” on WhatsApp hires a student to “test a Crystal Stones earnings dApp.” Pay is in CST. The student must not tell the academy. After three small “withdrawals” that actually arrive, a 400 USDT cash-out is frozen until a 60 USDT AML fee.

1. Secrets + earnings + do-not-tell was enough on day one. The small withdrawals were bait, not proof of a job.
2. Paying 60 USDT is a second donation, not a tax to a regulator. Regulators do not collect AML fees to a personal BEP-20 address in a chat.
3. The student stops. They do not recruit a cousin to “help complete the tasks.” Recruiting is how task mills become community.
4. If any of their own funds remain on the painted site, those funds were never on a chain they control. Chasing them is how the rest follows. Module 5.

DIAGRAM
Kindness / job / crush
        |
        v
Private platform or task mill
        |
        v
Small withdrawal works   <-- bait
        |
        v
Large one needs a fee    <-- the point
        |
        v
Stop. Do not pay. Do not recruit.
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
We are not mocking loneliness or unemployment. We are naming the script. If you are already in it, stop depositing, do not pay unfreeze taxes, talk to someone offline you already knew. Module 5 is incident response, not shame. Police recovery is not promised. Leftover dust is not a tracing fee.
ENDNOTE

A painted withdrawal that “needs 24 hours” is still a switch. A job that needs your KYC-facing exchange to receive “client USDT” is mule work even if the HR voice is kind. Kindness is cheap. Your name on a stolen pipe is not. If a recruiter says the academy secretly runs the desk, open the bookmarked LMS. If it is not published there, it is not a partnership. It is this module using our crystal as a prop.

## What this lesson is for

So that a small success stops being evidence. Scammers can afford a 20 USDT withdrawal. They cannot afford you walking away before the invoice. Walking away is the skill. If HR wants your silence, that silence is the product. A real job can survive a bookmark. A funnel cannot.

## Say this out loud

- Early small withdrawals can be bait. They are not an audit of a job.
- A lover who is also my broker is a script. Patience is part of the product.
- “Don’t tell the academy” plus earnings is a no, without a whitepaper.
- AML unfreeze fees to a chat address are donations. I do not pay them.
- I will not forward other people’s coins for a cut. That can make my KYC a mule pipe.

If a small withdrawal already arrived, that is not proof you should pay a tax. That is proof they can afford bait. Stop. Offline human. No recruit.

Next: admins, recovery specialists, and screen share — the second predator who arrives after you are already hurt.

lessons.title: Admins, recovery specialists, and screen share
lessons.content:
# Admins, recovery specialists, and screen share

When you are already hurt, a second predator arrives selling **recovery**. They watched the group. They can be in your DMs ninety seconds after you type “I got hacked.” Speed is not competence. Speed is a hunting pattern.

By the end of this lesson you should refuse recovery-for-seed, refuse a verify-bot, refuse screen share on a funded device, and treat leftover dust as bait, not as a tracing fee.

## Recovery specialists

“I work with the FBI / EFCC / Binance / BSC validators. Pay 2 BNB, I trace.” Tracing public transactions is something **you** can do on bookmarked BscScan. Paying them is a second donation.

Anyone who needs a seed to “trace” is the thief. Anyone who needs you to send leftover dust “so the trace can attach” is the thief. Anyone who needs remote control “to freeze the destination” is the thief. Validators do not run a consumer helpdesk that unsends a valid transfer. This academy will never DM you a recovery agent.

Law enforcement, if you use them, is a local process with a real office — not a Telegram handle, not a WhatsApp voice note, not a person who already knows your loss because they live in the same group. We will not pretend every stolen 20 USDT will be recovered. We will pretend 0% of seed-sharing recoveries are honest.

## Group admins and verify-bots

They mute you unless you “verify wallet.” They drop a bot. The bot wants a seed or a connect-and-approve. Real moderation does not need keys. Real moderation does not need unlimited USDT allowance to “prove you are human.”

If you are an admin, the pressure to “just add a verify bot” will come from a helper. That helper wants the room. Guard admin rights. Do not install mystery bots. Do not pin APKs.

If you were muted until you connected, leave the group. Muting is not a court. A community that cannot moderate without keys is not a community you owe a gun to. Take the bookmark you already had. Leave the bot.

## Screen share

AnyDesk, TeamViewer, “Google Meet, share the phone,” “I will drive, you watch.” They will open the wallet while you look away, or they will watch 2FA, or they will paste a destination you will confirm because a competent voice is speaking. There is no academy procedure that requires remote control of a funded device. There is no nonce repair that requires it. There is no Crystal Stones listing that requires it.

If a device must be repaired, you repair it without a funded wallet on screen, or you move funds to a new wallet on a clean device first. Helpers who cannot work under that rule are not helpers.

TABLE
Offer | Translation | Door
Trace for a fee + seed | Theft | Device
Trace for leftover dust | Second donation | Human + send
Admin verify-bot | Theft | Device or chain permission
Screen share to fix nonce / freeze / listing | Theft of session or keys | Device + account
“I will hold the funds and send back clean” | Theft or mule | Human
“FBI case ID, pay to open” | Costume | Human
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** A student lost 80 USDT to a clone. A recovery admin appears in 90 seconds (they watch the group). Case ID. Photo of a badge. “Send 0.2 BNB and the remaining dust so we can attach a tracer. Also share screen, faster.”

1. The student pays nothing. Dust stays. Screen stays unshared. Seed stays on paper, untyped.
2. They open bookmarked BscScan and write the drain hash in a notebook. That is the whole “trace.”
3. They follow Module 5 for remaining funds if any remain. They do not follow the admin.
4. They are down 80 USDT. They are not down 80 USDT and 0.2 BNB and a leaked seed. The second line was optional. Optional is the lesson.

DIAGRAM
Loss
  |
  +--> official ticket / local police if it makes sense for the amount and the place
  +--> bookmarked explorer, write hashes
  +--> remaining funds, clean device, name the door
  |
  X paid recovery in chat
  X seed
  X dust as tracing fee
  X screen share
  X "hold funds and send back clean"
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
This academy is not a law firm and not a recovery desk. Local rules differ. We only insist you do not add a crime, a screen share, a seed paste, or a second drain to the story. Do not send leftover dust to specialists. Do not promise yourself a police reversal the chain cannot do.
ENDNOTE

If you run a group, pin this lesson instead of a verify-bot. Speed-to-help after a drain is a hunting pattern you now recognise. The pinned text can say: remaining funds, bookmarks, no seed, no screen share, no dust. That pin will not make you support staff. It will make the second predator work harder.

## What this lesson is for

So that the minute after a loss is not a second loss. The first predator took a slice. The second predator takes the rest, plus the seed, plus the audience if they hijack your account while you share a screen. If you must help a friend in that minute, sit with them while they tap bookmarks. Do not drive. Driving is screen share with extra kindness.

## Say this out loud

- Recovery-for-seed is theft. I can read a hash on BscScan myself.
- Leftover dust is not a tracing fee. I will not send it to a specialist.
- Screen share on a funded phone is a no. There is no academy procedure that requires it.
- Verify-bots and mute-until-you-connect are Door 1 or Door 3 in a moderator hat.
- Second predators hunt first losses. Speed in the group is a hunting pattern, not competence.

If you are the friend sitting next to the loss, you still do not drive the phone. Bookmarks, remaining funds, no seed. Kindness that takes the wheel is screen share in a softer voice.

Next: guarantees, VIP rooms, and “the last train” — pressure language that should make you walk without a debate.

lessons.title: Guarantees, VIP rooms, and “the last train”
lessons.content:
# Guarantees, VIP rooms, and “the last train”

Pressure language is Door 4 in a tuxedo. It does not need a fake domain if it can make you skip the domain check. It does not need a seed box if it can make you send.

By the end of this lesson you should treat “guaranteed,” “last train,” “VIP after you recruit,” and “secret official contract” as walk-away phrases — not as a research assignment you must finish in eleven minutes.

## Words that fail the adult test

- guaranteed 10% a day, guaranteed listing, guaranteed recovery
- risk-free, insured by the chain, insured by the academy
- last train / closing in 11 minutes / snapshot in 8 minutes
- secret listing, send now, the academy is late, use this contract
- VIP room after you recruit three people
- “this is how the rich enter; Basic is for tourists”

Markets, if you ever meet them in Intermediate, do not talk like this. Criminal funnels do. A **guarantee** is a promise that physics and counterparties have been suspended for you. Adults hear a tell. Beginners hear a relief.

You do not need a whitepaper to refuse. Refusal is allowed to be short. “No” is a complete review.

If you want to go faster, finish Basic quizzes, use Mentor **in the app** with questions about concepts, not “what coin tonight.” Speed that skips Safety is how the last train leaves with your USDT. Ambition that requires a secret contract is not ambition. It is a funnel using your hurry as fuel.

## VIP rooms and recruitment

A room that requires you to bring people is a shape you already know from other decades: a pyramid with extra dashboards. Even when a token is real, a social funnel that pays you to recruit is not “community.” It is a business model that needs new deposits more than it needs your understanding.

This academy is an LMS. Progress is quizzes. Certificates are platform records. There is no VIP rail that skips Safety if you pay a handler in USDT. Speed that skips this course is how the last train leaves with your balance.

Recruitment pressure also hijacks friendships. If a lesson costs you a cousin’s rent, it was not a lesson. It was a funnel using your face (loot type: audience).

## “The academy is late, use this contract”

Clone plus cortisol. The public Crystal Stones contract, as the project publishes it, is `0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00` on BNB Smart Chain, chain id **56**. Verify on bookmarked BscScan. A VIP room’s “new official” born forty minutes ago, liquidity unlocked, name similar, is a clone. You do not owe it a swap. This paragraph is still not a buy order for the real one.

TABLE
Phrase | Adult translation | Move
Guaranteed return | They need you to believe variance is optional | Walk
Last train / 11 minutes | Cortisol prop | Walk; bookmarks still work in 20 minutes
VIP after you recruit | Pyramid shape | Walk; do not donate your cousins
Secret official contract | Clone | Bookmarked explorer, or nothing
Academy is late | Impersonation | Bookmarked LMS, or nothing
Risk-free crypto | A sentence that has never been true here | Walk
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** A VIP room shares a BSC token born 40 minutes ago, liquidity pool unlocked, name similar to Crystal Stones. “Last train. Academy people are sleeping.” A student who finished **this** lesson opens bookmarked BscScan instead of the swap.

1. They see the age of the contract. They see a name collision. They do not need a thread of 200 messages.
2. They go offline. They do not argue in the VIP room. Argument keeps Door 4 open.
3. They do not “just try 5 USDT to see.” Practice amounts are for learning rails, not for funding clones on purpose.
4. Sunday, they still have a play pocket. Intermediate is still optional. Solvency is the whole win.

DIAGRAM
Urgency + guarantee + secret + recruit
        |
        v
        No

You do not need a whitepaper to refuse.
You do not need to defeat the room in argument.
You need to leave the room.
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
Refusing does not make you “not ambitious.” It makes you still solvent for Intermediate. This academy will not punish you for walking out of a funnel. It will also not congratulate a clone for being fast. Fast is easy when you are stealing.
ENDNOTE

If the room is also your only “market news,” you will feel uninformed when you leave. That feeling is the product. Bookmarked BscScan, the academy LMS, and a Sunday checklist are slower news and still news. Missing a forty-minute-old clone is not a career wound. Catching it with a swap is.

## What this lesson is for

So that pressure is visible as pressure. You already have panic-day steps. This is the social version: no timer, no VIP, no secret contract, no recruitment homework. If leaving a room costs you a friend, that friendship was the funnel. You can still be kind. You cannot be their downline.

## Say this out loud

- Guarantees are a tell. Markets do not talk like that; funnels do.
- Last-train timers are props. If it would still be real in twenty minutes, I start from a bookmark.
- Secret official contracts are clones. I verify `0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00` on bookmarked BscScan, or I verify nothing.
- VIP-after-recruit is a pyramid shape. I will not donate my cousins.
- I can refuse without a debate. “No” is a complete review.

You do not owe the room a thread. Leaving unread is allowed. A clone will not become honest because you explained Safety to it.

Next: pig butchering and investment-club folklore — the long con named calmly, so the story is harder to run on you or on someone you love.

lessons.title: Pig butchering and investment-club folklore, named calmly
lessons.content:
# Pig butchering and investment-club folklore, named calmly

**Pig butchering** is a documented crime pattern with a cruel name. We use the name because you will meet it in news and in group chats. The idea is calm: fatten trust, then slaughter the savings. It is not a joke about victims. It is a map.

By the end of this lesson you should recognise the long-con calendar, distinguish a painted platform from a bookmarked exchange, and refuse investment-club folklore that needs your silence, your friends, and a guaranteed number.

## The calendar, not the movie

Week 1–2: a wrong-number text, a comment on a post, a friendly stranger who is not in a hurry. They talk about food, work, faith, gym, children. They do not talk about USDT.

Week 3–6: competence and warmth. They have a “mentor” or they *are* learning a “safe desk.” They screen-share profits. The numbers are pretty. They still do not need your money.

Week 6+: a private website, an app from a link, a “licensed” desk you cannot find on a bookmark you already had. Small deposit. Small withdrawal **works**. Larger deposit. Withdrawal stuck. Tax, AML, upgrade, insurance, last train. Then a recovery specialist. You have met every costume in this module, in order.

The patience is expensive for them. It is cheap compared to one person’s year of work. That is why it exists.

## Painted platforms versus rails you already know

A **painted platform** is a website that shows numbers. It is not BscScan. It is not the bookmarked exchange you already have an account on. Withdrawals are a switch an operator flips. When they flip it off, no explorer will help you, because your USDT may already have left to them on the first deposit.

If someone will only trade with you on a site they sent, and they become angry when you suggest a bookmarked major exchange or — better — not trading with a lover at all, you have the tell. Anger at a bookmark is not passion. It is operational security for a funnel.

Investment-club folklore sits next door: “we are twenty families, we have a desk, 8% a week, keep it quiet, bring your auntie.” Community is real. Guaranteed yield is not. Clubs that require recruitment are often pyramids. Clubs that require a painted site plus silence are often pig butchering with extra uncles.

This academy is not an investment club. Basic is rails. Intermediate, if you continue, is still education — contracts, DeFi, tokenomics — and will still refuse guaranteed profit.

TABLE
Folklore | What is actually happening | What you do
Wrong-number friend who becomes your broker | Long con calendar | Do not deposit; talk offline to someone you already knew
Private app with pretty profits | Painted switch, not a public book | Demand a bookmark you already had, or walk
Small withdraw then AML tax | Bait then invoice | Stop; do not pay
Family investment club, guaranteed, recruit | Pyramid or a painted desk | Walk; do not bring auntie
“Recovery team” after the slaughter | Second predator | Module 3 lesson 4, then Module 5
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** An auntie in Lagos has a new friend from a “wrong SMS.” After a month the friend teaches her a private app. She withdraws 30,000 local currency-equivalent once. She deposits much more. Stuck. The friend introduces a recovery officer. The officer wants a seed and the remaining dust.

1. A niece who finished this course sits with her, not above her. Shame is how the con continues. Calm naming is how it stops.
2. They do not pay the recovery officer. They do not type words. They do not install the officer’s APK.
3. They photograph nothing of a seed. They may write hashes if any on-chain sends exist, for a local report if the family chooses. No promise that police will reverse the chain.
4. They warn two other family groups with the *domain* and the *script*, not with the auntie’s remaining wallet as a bounty.

DIAGRAM
Warmth without money
        |
        v
Private painted desk
        |
        v
Small out  (bait)
        |
        v
Large in
        |
        v
Stuck + tax + recovery costume
        |
        v
Stop deposits. No seed. No dust. Offline human.
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
If this lesson is arriving late — if the painted site already has a number you cannot stand to lose — Module 5 is next after this module’s quiz. Saving remaining funds is not “giving up on them.” Chasing a painted withdrawal is how remaining funds join the painting. You are not owed a Hollywood ending. You are owed a clear sentence: the switch is theirs.
ENDNOTE

Investment-club folklore will borrow this academy’s name. “Crystal Stones families, 8% a week, keep it quiet.” Quiet plus a number plus recruitment is the tell, not the crystal. Teach the calendar without cruelty. Sit with the person. Do not become their new broker. Do not become their recovery officer. Become the human who names the switch.

## What this lesson is for

So that a slow kindness stops looking like proof. So that you can sit with someone you love and name a calendar without cruelty. So that investment-club folklore cannot borrow this academy’s crystal as a guarantee.

## Say this out loud

- Pig butchering is a long-con calendar: warmth, painted desk, small out, large in, tax, fake recovery.
- A private platform a lover sent is not BscScan and not a bookmarked exchange.
- Guaranteed club yield plus recruitment is folklore I will not bring auntie into.
- I will not pay an unfreeze tax or send leftover dust to finish a slaughter.
- Shame keeps the script running. A calm name and an offline human stop the next deposit.

Take the quiz. Module 4: on-chain drains — approvals, poison tokens, permits, revoke without a second drainer, and reading the loss on BscScan.

lessons.title: Approvals are loaded guns
lessons.content:
# Approvals are loaded guns

You met this on the BNB Smart Chain course. Here we treat it as a crime scene, not as a glossary line.

An **approval** is an on-chain message to a token contract: spender S may take up to N of my tokens. A **spender** is usually another contract — a DEX router, a bridge, a “launchpad,” or a drainer. DEX routers need this to pull in what you swap. Drainers need this to pull **everything later**.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to say what unlimited means, why a later drain may have no Send popup, and why a dashboard that wants unlimited USDT to *view* Crystal Stones is hostile.

## What you actually signed

Tokens like USDT on BEP-20, and Crystal Stones as a BEP-20 token, follow a common pattern: your wallet does not always “send” the token in one step when a site swaps it. The site’s contract **pulls**. The permission to pull is the approval.

**Unlimited** means N is enormous — often `2^256-1`, shown in the UI as “unlimited” or “infinite.” Convenient. If the spender is evil, or later gets hacked, or later sells its keys, they do not need you again.

**Finite** means you approve only a little more than this swap. Annoying. You will sign more often. You will survive a future drainer better. Annoyance is a fee. Unlimited is a loaded gun with no extra click.

Connect Wallet is not Approve. Viewing a token is not Approve. Adding a custom token is not Approve. If a “dashboard” insists on unlimited USDT to **view** Crystal Stones, leave. Viewing is a read. Reads do not need a gun.

A common costume: “allow once to prove you are not a bot.” Bots do not hold your USDT. You do. Another: “this is the same as Connect.” It is not. Read the popup’s verb. If the verb is Approve, Permit, Increase allowance, or Set approval for all, you are loading a gun, even if the site header says Welcome.

## You will not see a “Send” when they collect

Days later, a function named `transferFrom` can run. Your wallet may not popup. You may be asleep. BscScan will show the spender as the actor, not a second signature from you that night. People say “I didn’t click Send.” Correct. They clicked **Approve** last month.

This is why “I would notice” is not a control. The noticing was supposed to happen at approve time: network, asset, spender, amount, site bookmark. After that, the gun is loaded until you **revoke** (next lessons) or until they fire.

If the seed is also leaked, they do not even need the gun. They can send directly. Approvals are Door 3. Seeds are Door 1. Do not mix the post-mortems.

TABLE
UI text | Adult meaning | What later looks like
Allow USDT to spend / Approve | Loaded gun for that spender | transferFrom while you sleep
Unlimited / infinite | No extra click later | One fire can empty the pocket
Exact amount for this swap | Gun with one magazine | They cannot take more than you loaded, from this approve
Revoke / set allowance to 0 | Unload | Costs a little BNB; worth it
Connect Wallet | Handshake with a site | Not permission to take tokens
Add token / view balance | A display | If they demand unlimited to view, leave
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** In March a student approved unlimited USDT to a “launchpad” that looked like a listing for Crystal Stones. In August the launchpad key leaks — or was always evil. USDT leaves at 03:12. The seed is still in the student’s phone.

1. Door 3, not Door 1, until proven otherwise. They still rotate if the device might be dirty (Module 5), because phones that visit launchpads are not always clean.
2. They do not go to the launchpad site to Disconnect. That button does not unload the chain.
3. They revoke from a bookmarked checker, then move remaining funds if any remain.
4. They still did not have to click Send for the drain. That sentence is the one they teach a cousin.

DIAGRAM
Approve unlimited
        |
        v
Time passes (days, months)
        |
        v
transferFrom from the spender
        |
        v
Wallet may not popup
Explorer will still show the spender

Viewing a token never needed this gun.
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
This academy will not tell you to approve Crystal Stones, USDT, or anything else. Education only. If you ever approve on purpose, finite is the adult default, on a site you bookmarked, for a swap you meant. Unlimited for convenience is how August inherits March.
ENDNOTE

If a wallet UI hides the word unlimited behind “default,” tap the amount and read it. Defaults are how convenience loads guns. Changing a default to a finite number is a thirty-second adult habit. If the site refuses to work without unlimited, the site is not a swap you needed. Leave.

## What this lesson is for

So that “I didn’t send” stops being a mystery. You loaded a spender. The book will say so. The book is how you stop guessing, and how you pick revoke versus rotate. Convenience is not a third option. Unlimited for “I will be back” is how you come back to an empty pocket.

## Say this out loud

- An approval loads a spender. Unlimited means they may not need me later.
- A drain can happen via transferFrom without a new Send popup.
- Connect, add token, and view are not approve. A dashboard that needs unlimited USDT to view is hostile.
- Fake-site Disconnect does not unload the gun. Revoke is a later, bookmarked job.
- Door 3 is not Door 1. I still treat a dirty device as a reason to rotate.

If a site cannot swap without unlimited, you did not need that swap. Finite or leave. Convenience is how August inherits March.

Next: poison tokens, fake airdrops, and bait NFTs — junk that arrives uninvited with a URL in the name.

lessons.title: Poison tokens, fake airdrops, and bait NFTs
lessons.content:
# Poison tokens, fake airdrops, and bait NFTs

Anyone can send junk to your address. The send is a **notification** with a hook. It is not a salary. It is not proof you are early. It is not Crystal Stones arriving as a gift from the academy.

By the end of this lesson you should hide unsolicited tokens, refuse URLs in token names, and not approve a “convert / claim / clean blacklist” site you just met.

## Zero-value tokens and fake millions

They appear in the wallet list with a huge fake USD price. The hook is often a website in the token name: “Visit claim-cst-drainer.tld.” You tap, connect, approve. Door 3, sometimes Door 1 if they also ask for a seed.

The USD figure is a costume. Wallet apps guess prices from thin or fictional markets. A day-old contract with no honest liquidity can still display eight million dollars. Display is not money. **Liquidity**, in the street sense you need today, means: there are actually other people willing to take the other side of a trade at a price that is not a cartoon. A bookmarked BscScan token page will show age, holders, and whether anyone real is there. You still do not need to visit the URL in the name. You still do not need to “sell it on the site it suggested.” Selling is a swap. Swaps need approvals. Approvals are the hook.

There is no penalty for hiding. Wallet apps (Trust Wallet and MetaMask remain **examples**) have a hide or spam control. Use it. The junk can sit on the chain forever. Your BNB does not leak merely because a stranger sent you a row. Signing is how you accept a job you were not offered.

## Bait NFTs

Same family. “You are blacklisted, clean here.” “Security update, mint to keep your wallet.” “Crystal Stones founder pass.” Cleaning is the drain. **setApprovalForAll** — permission for an operator to take NFTs — is the usual gun. If you do not collect NFTs on purpose, you have no reason to sign that.

If you *do* collect NFTs on purpose, you still bookmark the market, still read the popup, still refuse operators you cannot name. A founder-pass that arrived uninvited is not a collection. It is bait with a picture.

## Airdrop, two honest sentences

A real **airdrop**, when it exists, is usually tokens that simply appear, or a claim on a site you already bookmarked before the drama. It does not need a seed. It does not need unlimited USDT. It does not need you to pay a helper for gas. It does not expire in eight minutes on a banner.

Unsolicited inbound is, for your purposes, hostile until it is boring. Hide it. Your BNB and USDT are not automatically in danger **until you sign**. The junk can sit there forever. There is no penalty for ignoring a gift. There is a penalty for being polite to it.

People fail this lesson because the wallet UI is designed like a shop: new row, big number, bright icon. Shops want you to tap. Attackers rent that habit. A second failure is social: you ask a fan group “is this the official airdrop?” The group contains the helper with the claim link. You already had the rule before you asked. Asking was Door 4 inviting a costume.

A third failure is “I’ll just connect, I won’t approve.” Clone sites queue the signature after connect, and tired people remember the connect, not the sign. Hide is cheaper than a careful connect. A fourth is “I’ll sell it on PancakeSwap so it doesn’t clutter.” Selling a mystery token is how you visit a router you did not mean, on a pair with no honest liquidity, and load a gun besides.

TABLE
Inbox junk | Safe response | Unsafe response
Fake million with a URL in the name | Hide / ignore | Visit the URL, connect, approve
NFT from nowhere | Hide | “Clean blacklist,” setApprovalForAll
“You are hacked, revoke here” as a token symbol | Bookmark a known revoke tool later, not this URL | Enter the symbol’s website
Lookalike Crystal Stones | Verify `0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00` on bookmarked BscScan, or ignore | Swap it on a site the token suggested
Poison dust of BNB or USDT from a lookalike address | Leave it; do not copy that from-address later | Use history as an address book
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** A wallet shows +$8,000,000 CrystalStonesAirdrop. A student feels rich and also “should claim before it expires.” That emotion is the payload.

1. Bookmarked BscScan token page: a day-old contract, no honest liquidity, name collision with Crystal Stones. Not `0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00`.
2. They hide the token in the wallet app (Trust Wallet and MetaMask are **examples of wallet apps**; the hide control lives in the app, not on a claim site).
3. Stack of real USDT and BNB unchanged. No approve. No visit.
4. They do not ask the fan group “is this real?” because the group will contain a helper with a claim link. They already have the rule.

DIAGRAM
Unsolicited inbound
        |
        +--> hide
        |
        X visit URL in the name
        X approve to convert
        X setApprovalForAll to clean
        X ask a fan group while the timer runs
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
“Airdrop token in the wallet is free money” is a quiz answer this course will fail. Unsolicited tokens are notifications. Free money that needs a signature is priced at whatever the spender can pull. You already know the price can be the whole pocket.
ENDNOTE

## What this lesson is for

So that inbound junk stops feeling like a decision. The decision was made by a stranger. Your job is hide. Signing is how you accept a job you were not offered.

## Say this out loud

- Unsolicited tokens are notifications, not assets. A fake USD figure is a costume.
- URLs in token names are hostile. I do not visit them.
- Hide, do not hunt. I am not rude for ignoring a gift.
- “Clean blacklist” and “claim airdrop” sites I just met are Door 3.
- Real Crystal Stones, if I ever verify it, is a known contract on bookmarked BscScan — not a surprise million.

Next: “Sign to verify,” permits, and typed data — signatures that are not a Send and still move authority.

lessons.title: Sign to verify, permits, and typed data
lessons.content:
# Sign to verify, permits, and typed data

Not every signature is a gas-paying transaction. **Off-chain signatures** can still move authority. The wallet says “Sign.” People hear “login.” Drainers hear “yes.”

By the end of this lesson you should reject hex blobs, treat **permits** as approvals in a costume, and never sign to verify a Mentor, a listing, or a freeze appeal.

## Login signatures

Many sites: “Sign to prove you own this address.” If the message is literally a human sentence on a **bookmarked** site — “Log in to example.com at 12:04” — risk is lower. They can still impersonate you **on that site**. They usually cannot, from that message alone, pull USDT. Still do not sign on a clone. Still do not sign if you did not bookmark the host.

Lower risk is not zero. It is “maybe.” Maybe is allowed to wait.

If the site is a clone of this academy, of BscScan, or of an exchange, the login signature is still a no — because you should not be proving ownership to a thief’s server at all. They can use that session to show you a second popup (the permit) while you think you are already “in.” Two signatures, one costume. Reject the first if the host is not a bookmark.

## Permits (EIP-2612 style) and cousins

A **permit** is a signature that says the token may treat a spender as approved **without** a separate approve transaction. The next transaction from the attacker pulls funds. You saw “Sign,” not “Approve.” You still opened Door 3.

Wallet UIs vary. Some show the word Permit. Some show typed fields: token, spender, value, deadline. Some show a wall of hex. If value looks unlimited, it is unlimited. If you cannot see value, you do not sign.

Related costumes: `increaseAllowance`, `setApprovalForAll`, typed data that mentions a spender you did not intend, “Sign to claim” on a site you met today.

## Hardware does not decode tiredness

A hardware wallet will happily sign a permit if you confirm. The device is a yes-machine for whatever you allow. Read the screen. If the screen is a blob you cannot parse, reject. “Hardware wallet means I can sign anything blindly” is a failed quiz on purpose. Tired is a reason to close the laptop, not a reason to tap.

## How to refuse, as a habit

If the wallet’s message is a wall of hex, reject. If it says Permit, increaseAllowance, setApprovalForAll, transfer, or swap on a site you did not intend, reject. If a “Crystal Mentor verify” page wants a signature, reject — real Mentor in the academy app never needed that. If you cannot decode it, **reject**. There is no prize for signing under confusion.

TABLE
Prompt | Default | Why
Sign in to a bookmarked site with a human-readable message | Maybe | Site-login risk, not usually a token gun
Permit unlimited USDT / CST | No | Door 3 in a costume
Hex blob you cannot read | No | You cannot name the loot
setApprovalForAll | No unless you fully intend that NFT market, bookmarked | Operator gun for NFTs
“Sign to verify / unfreeze / list / mint certificate” | No | Academy and honest explorers do not work this way
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** A “Crystal Mentor verify” page (fake) asks for a signature. The wallet shows typed data mentioning USDT and a spender. A student almost signs because the academy crystal is in the tab icon.

1. They reject. Real Mentor, inside the bookmarked academy app, never needed a USDT permit.
2. They do not try to “finish verification” with a smaller signature. There is no smaller yes that satisfies a drainer.
3. They open the real app. Progress is still there. Certificates in Basic are platform records after quizzes, not a wallet event.
4. If they had signed, Module 5 plus a revoke from a bookmark — not a return to the verify page.

DIAGRAM
Sign popup
   |
   +--> readable login on a bookmark?  maybe
   +--> permit / hex / operator / unfreeze?  reject
   +--> tired / cannot decode?  reject
   |
   Hardware
   --> still reject if the device screen is a blob
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
Signing “to be polite” is how people empty a play pocket and then a savings pocket if those pockets share a seed. Politeness is for humans you know offline. Machines get reject. This academy will never ask you to sign typed data to prove you are a student.
ENDNOTE

If a site says “this signature does nothing, it just verifies,” read the fields anyway. “Does nothing” is a sentence in English. The wallet is showing mathematics. Mathematics wins. If your app cannot show typed fields and only shows hex, that app is the wrong tool for that site, or the site is the wrong site. Either way: reject, bookmark, later.

## What this lesson is for

So that Sign stops being a synonym for harmless. You name the loot, or you reject. Confusion is not a maybe. Confusion is a no. A Mentor, listing, certificate, or freeze page that wants typed data is a costume even when the crystal looks right. Real Mentor stays in the bookmarked app and does not need USDT permission.

## Say this out loud

- Sign is not harmless by default. Permits are approvals in a costume.
- Hex blobs get a no. If I cannot decode it, I reject.
- Crystal Mentor, certificates, and freeze appeals do not need a USDT signature.
- Hardware wallets still require me to read the device. Blind confirm is Door 3 with extra steel.
- Tired people should not sign. Closing the laptop is a complete procedure.

“Sign to verify” is not a greeting. If Crystal Mentor, a listing desk, or a freeze appeal wants typed data, it is a costume. Real Mentor stays in the app.

Next: revoking approvals without walking into a second drainer — including the revoke site that asks for a seed first.

lessons.title: Revoking approvals without a second drain
lessons.content:
# Revoking approvals without a second drain

**Revoke** means sending a new transaction that sets allowance for that spender to 0. It costs a little BNB. It is worth it. It is also a hunting ground: people google “revoke approval” while their hands shake, tap the first ad, and sign a second gun.

By the end of this lesson you should bookmark a checker on a calm day, revoke unknown unlimited spenders when the seed is still yours, and walk away from any revoke site that asks for a seed first.

## Use a tool you bookmarked on a calm day

Common explorers have token-approval checkers (BscScan token approval pages and well-known revoke UIs). Bookmark from documentation you trust **before** you are on fire. This academy will not paste a random revoke URL in a lesson that will rot. Your calm-day job is to save **one** from BscScan’s own docs or UI. If you cannot do that yet, wait for a knowledgeable human **offline** rather than an ad.

Googling “revoke approval” + the first ad is how the second drainer greets you. A revoke site that asks for a **seed** first is not a revoke site. Revoke is an on-chain transaction your wallet already on the device can sign. Seeds are for restoring a wallet, not for listing spenders. Seed-first is Door 1 wearing a hygiene costume.

## Procedure, when Door 1 is probably still shut

1. Open the **bookmarked** checker. Confirm the host still matches the bookmark. Panic fingers lie.
2. Connect — this is a rare time connect is required. You are talking to a read tool so it can query your address. Still confirm the URL.
3. List spenders on USDT, other BEP-20 tokens you actually hold, Crystal Stones if you hold it.
4. Revoke unknown or unlimited you do not need. Finite leftover on a DEX you still use can wait for a calm reduction, or you can zero it and re-approve finite next swap.
5. Confirm each revoke transaction on bookmarked BscScan. The book should show allowance going toward zero.
6. Disconnect in the wallet app. You still do not return to a fake site to Disconnect.

## What revoke does not fix

- they already `transferFrom`’d — that money is gone
- they have the seed — they will approve again from another device; rotation is the job (Module 5)
- the device is malware-soaked — they may sign a new approve while you revoke; clean device, then rotate
- a malicious **owner** of a junk token you still “hold” — do not visit claim sites to bring junk along; hide it; move understood assets

If Door 1 might be open, revoke on a still-leaked seed is theatre. New wallet, test, move, retire. You may still revoke on the old address after, if you like a tidy book. Tidy is not safety if they still have the words.

TABLE
State | Action | Not the action
Unknown unlimited spender, seed safe, device reasonably clean | Revoke from bookmarked checker | Ad; seed-first site
Spender already drained, seed safe | Revoke leftovers; move remaining if device is dirty | Pay a tracer
Seed maybe leaked | New wallet on clean device; test; move; retire old | Revoke as the only step
Revoke UI asks for 12 words | Close tab; treat as Door 1 attempt | “Just this once, it’s hygiene”
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** A student used a real DEX months ago (legitimate router still approved unlimited). Sunday checklist. They reduce to zero. Next swap they will approve a finite amount. Annoyance is the fee of Door 3 hygiene.

A second student googles “revoke BSC” the night of a scare. The ad asks them to import a seed “to scan allowances.” They almost do, because support-shaped language said “required to help.” They remember this paragraph. They close the tab. They wait until morning and use a bookmark.

DIAGRAM
Calm day: bookmark a real approval checker from explorer docs / UI
Fire day: use that bookmark, not an ad
Seed-first revoke site: close
If seed leaked: skip to rotation, do not perform theatre
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
Revoke costs BNB. Keep a little native coin on the play pocket for this reason. If you have no BNB and a loaded gun, that is a reason to get practice-size BNB through a path you already trust — not a reason to accept “we will pay gas if you share the seed.”
ENDNOTE

Do not revoke *from* the drainer’s own “security portal.” Their portal is how they collect the next permit while you think you are unloading the last one. Bookmark, host name, then connect. If your hands shake, wait. A gun that has not fired can wait an hour. A second gun cannot. Unlimited leftover on a router you “might use someday” is how someday arrives as a headline. Zero is allowed to be annoying.

## What this lesson is for

So that hygiene does not become a second crime scene. Revoke is ordinary. Seed-first revoke is a robbery. Ads are Door 3 in a cape. If you finish a revoke and the checker still shows the spender, wait for the explorer confirmation, then refresh. Do not “try a different revoke site” from search. That is how the second gun loads while you chase a UI lag.

## Say this out loud

- Revoke is an on-chain allowance-to-zero. It costs a little BNB. It does not need a seed.
- I bookmark the checker before I need it. I do not google revoke into ads on a fire day.
- A revoke site that asks for a seed first is a thief.
- Revoke does not fix a leaked seed. They will approve again. I rotate.
- Fake-site Disconnect is not revoke.

If the checker lags, wait on the bookmarked explorer. Do not hunt a second revoke UI from an ad. Lag is cheaper than a second gun.

Next: reading a drain on BscScan so you can name the door from the book, not from a group chat.

lessons.title: Reading a drain on BscScan so you stop guessing
lessons.content:
# Reading a drain on BscScan so you stop guessing

When USDT leaves, the book still talks. Guessing in a group chat hands the story to impersonators. The explorer, from a bookmark, is slower and ruder and true.

By the end of this lesson you should classify a loss as a wrong send, an approval-then-pull, a hostile swap bundle, or a leaked key — and write hashes in a notebook instead of a recovery DM.

## Four patterns

**A. Honest send to a wrong address.** `to` is an EOA you do not own. Token transfer matches what you remember signing. Paste attack, fake invoice, QR mismatch, wrong network sometimes. Door 4 plus a send. Seed may still be yours.

**B. Approval, later pull.** An earlier transaction is `approve` (or a permit). A later transaction from the spender runs `transferFrom` while you slept. Door 3. Seed may still be yours. Revoke and consider a fresh hot wallet if the device is dirty.

**C. Swap or router you did not mean.** `to` is a contract. One bundle empties the pocket — hops, wrapping, a spender you did not read. Door 3 or Door 4 plus a signature. Still maybe Door 1 if malware signed it.

**D. Seed leaked or malware signing.** Many transactions you **did not** click, from your EOA, including after you uninstalled the app. Transfers you do not remember. New approves you do not remember. This is Door 1. Rotate. Do not “repair” the old words.

Exchange-side: a withdrawal you did not start, while your on-chain address is quiet, is Door 2. That post-mortem lives on the company’s history page, from a bookmark, not only on BscScan.

TABLE
Clue | Likely door | First honest move
You remember the popup that night, destination wrong | Human + send | Remaining funds; do not send again to unlock
Approval then later pull while you slept | Chain permission | Revoke from bookmark if seed still yours
Txs you never signed, app uninstalled, still moving | Device (key leak or signing malware) | New seed on clean device; test; move; retire
CEX withdrawal you did not start, chain quiet | Account | Official security page: sessions, 2FA, whitelist
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** At 03:11 an approval to a new spender. At 03:12 USDT `transferFrom`. The student was asleep.

1. They open bookmarked BscScan on the address. They do not connect. They read.
2. They search last week’s history. There it is: a “claim” approve from a site they barely remember. Door 3. Not a mystery hack of BNB validators.
3. Seed maybe still theirs. Device maybe dirty. They revoke from a bookmark, then move remaining to a fresh hot wallet from a cleaner device anyway. Two pockets would have made this cheaper.
4. They write both hashes in a private notebook. They do not paste the remaining address into Telegram with a bounty. They do not send leftover dust to a tracer.

DIAGRAM
Open your address on bookmarked BscScan (no connect)
        |
        v
Find the first unexpected approve or send
        |
        v
That event names the door
        |
        v
Respond to that door
        |
        X recovery DM
        X second send to refund address
        X "I can outrun it if I am fast"
ENDDIAGRAM

## You cannot outrun a drain by paying the thief

A destination that says “refund” in a token name, or a helper who says “send the rest here to reverse,” is not a refund rail. Sending more is a second gift. Speed does not unsay a valid signature. The chain will settle the second gift as calmly as the first.

Write hashes. Hashes help a real police report if you file one locally. They do not help a Telegram wizard. This academy will not promise that a report brings USDT home. It will promise that a notebook is cheaper than a wizard.

Do not “watch the thief’s address” as a hobby the same night. Watching is how people send a test to a refund-looking twin and call it research. If you must look, look from the bookmark, once, write the hash, close the tab. Remaining funds do not need a live stream of the gone slice.

NOTE
If you cannot read BscScan yet, that is what the previous course was for. Re-open it. Do not hire a narrator in a DM. A cousin who finished Basic, sitting next to you, looking at a bookmark, is a narrator you can survive.
ENDNOTE

If the book is hard to read, slow down the labels: **from** (who started it), **to** (who received it), **method** (approve, transfer, transferFrom, swap), **token** (the contract, not the icon), **time**. Icons lie. Methods do not. Do not watch the thief’s address as a hobby the same night. Watching is how people send a test to a refund-looking twin and call it research.

## What this lesson is for

So that the book, not a costume, names the door. Naming picks Module 5’s procedure. Guessing picks Module 3’s second predator. If you only remember one explorer habit: paste the hash on a bookmark, do not connect, write it down. That habit survives tiredness. A wizard does not.

## Say this out loud

- The book shows whether it was a send, an approve-then-pull, a hostile bundle, or a leaked key.
- Sleep-time pulls often point at an earlier approve. Mystery signed txs point at Door 1 or malware.
- I cannot outrun a drain by sending to the thief’s refund address. That is a second gift.
- Hashes go in a notebook, not a recovery chat. Reports are optional and local. Reversal is not promised.
- I do not connect a wallet to an explorer to read a public hash.

Five labels are enough: from, to, method, token, time. Icons are costumes. A cousin on a bookmark beats a wizard in a DM.

Take the quiz. Module 5: if something already went wrong — the first hour, seed rotation, exchange sessions, reporting versus revenge, and what will not come back.
